title: architecture-datamodel reads architecture.md without declaring it
detail: Step 1 reads `10_blueprint/architecture.md` for module entities, but the prerequisites and `artifacts.requires` do not list it; only `06_behaviors` is declared (soft). `concept_structure.md` puts stack-specific schema files such as `schema.prisma` under `datamodel/`. The skill defers that translation to `build-database`, which takes the schema location from the template.

evidence.quote: Translating any of it into a stack is `build-database`'s step
that template's `## Migration / ORM` gives the schema file

recommendation: Declare `architecture.md` as a soft prerequisite of `architecture-datamodel`. Name one owner for the stack-specific schema file in `concept_structure.md`.

title: External integrations are recorded in techstack.md and architecture.md
detail: `architecture-techstack` writes `## Additional Integrations` (payments, mail, file storage) and shows the outside services at approval. `architecture-system` then asks about external services in step 3 and records them as `external_integrations`; its step 1 reads `techstack.md` only for `tech_stack_skill`. The `framework_experience` and `hosting` input fields repeat topics that step 3 asks again.

evidence.quote: which outside services it will talk to and what for
`## Additional Integrations` covering payments, mail and SMS

recommendation: Give integrations one home, `architecture.md`, and drop the section from `techstack.md`. Make step 3 skip every question that an input field already answered.

title: The entity-feature link is written twice: feature-map.json, data_entities[]
detail: Step 5 writes `feature-map.json` (model to feature files); step 7 writes `data_entities[]` into each feature (feature to models). That is one relation in two files, and `ops-review` and `feedback_loop.md` must keep the pair in sync. Step 4 also restates `seed_data.md` rules (timestamps, locales, string lengths) after it cites the contract.

evidence.quote: **Write `feature-map.json`**, mapping each model to the feature files it came
`data_entities[]` lists the entities that serve it
mapping each model to the features it serves
Set `data_entities:` to the list of model names

recommendation: Keep `data_entities[]` as the link and derive `feature-map.json` from it, or drop the file. In step 4, cite `seed_data.md` and delete the restated rules.

title: architecture-datamodel reads 7 inputs and cites 7 contracts
detail: Step 1 reads the features, `brief.md`, `glossary.md`, `techstack.md`, `stories.yaml`, `architecture.md` and `06_behaviors/`. The skill cites seven contracts; only `spec-feature` also cites seven, `ops-review` cites five. The glossary reconciliation (step 6) and the feature scan come from other stages (F08, F17).
recommendation: Move glossary pinning (F08) and the feature scan (F17) out of this skill. Cite contract sections, not whole files.

title: Hard gates require artifacts that four profiles say they never grow
detail: `cli-tool`, `api-service`, `library` and `data-pipeline` list `journeys` and `screens` under `not_grown`. `build-plan` and `build-implement` hard-gate `07_screens`; `spec-featuresets` and `quality-e2e` hard-gate `stories.yaml`. A search of `forge/` finds 0 uses of `not_grown`, so the host does not read it; in `appbuilder-mvp` no node produces `07_screens/`.

evidence.quote: has found a project shaped this way, not a gap to report
A declared path is joined to the *project* root

recommendation: Make gates on `not_grown` artifacts `soft` and state in the step what changes without them. Add a `check.py` rule that cross-checks hard gates against `profiles/*.yaml`.

title: The feature-to-commit link lives in three places, each read by another skill
detail: `build-implement` step 8 writes the commits twice: in the slice `index.md` and in the spec frontmatter. `ops-review` step 8 rebuilds them from the slice dossiers into `trace.yaml`. `quality-review` reads the frontmatter copy and `quality-release` reads `trace.yaml`. The spec is also reviewed twice: `build-implement` step 3 and the Spec axis of `quality-review`.

evidence.quote: frontmatter with the slice reference, the commit SHAs and the source files
the union of the commits and source files those slices recorded
**Review against the spec before reviewing the code.**
merging Standards and Spec into one ranked list

recommendation: Make `trace.yaml` the one derived join and let readers use it. Keep a single spec review, in `quality-review`.

title: Two skills flip acceptance-ledger rows with no overwrite rule
detail: `build-plan` creates the ledger; `build-implement` and `quality-e2e` both flip rows. `quality-review` and `ops-review` only read it. The contract says a skill flips only rows it evaluated, but not what happens when a row is already `PASS` or `FAIL`; `quality-e2e` also continues when no ledger exists.

evidence.quote: creates the file when it cuts the feature into slices
flips the rows its slice gate actually exercised
flips the rows a journey evaluated end to end
A skill flips only the rows it evaluated.
ledger is missing, warn and continue
The verdict file is the only thing this skill

recommendation: Add a rule to the contract: the later evaluation overwrites a row and stamps its own evidence, and `FAIL` beats `PASS`. Make `quality-e2e` stop when the ledger is missing.

title: build-plan names both decision files; build-branch is mostly git commands
detail: `build-plan` step 1 names `10_blueprint/decisions.md` and `11_build/decisions.md` by path, which `domain_model.md` already defines. `build-branch` adds two rules to plain git: the unlanded-slice check (step 5) and the typed word for merge and discard (step 7). The other steps are git commands.

evidence.quote: Merge and discard each need the word typed

recommendation: Cite `domain_model.md` in `build-plan` instead of naming both paths. State in `build-branch` that the two rules are its job.

title: Database and e2e results end in chat; scaffold and branch leave only git
detail: `build-database` step 9 and `quality-e2e` step 8 end with a chat report. Per-journey pass or fail reaches the ledger only through rows; screenshots stay in the codebase by design. `build-scaffold` and `build-branch` leave the scaffold approval and the chosen ending to git; ADR 0010 rejects a status file for the scaffold.

evidence.quote: **Run each scenario end to end, then report**
Screenshots are test output and live beside the tests in the
Approve, or name what to change and fix it here
the scaffold's record is its commit (ADR 0010)
Merge and discard each need the word typed

recommendation: Persist the per-journey verdict where `quality-release` can read it; `quality-release` re-walks the journeys today. Leave scaffold and branch to git, as ADR 0010 says.

title: quality-standards runs only in the reverse flow; build skills never read it
detail: `quality-standards` appears in `skaileup-concept-reverse` and in no other flow. It says code-writing skills read its index themselves, and its example lists `build-implement` and `build-plan` as readers. Among skills only `quality-review` names `02_grounding/standards/`, so in `appbuilder-*` the index never exists and neither build skill looks for it.

evidence.quote: skills that write code read `02_grounding/standards/index.yml` themselves when
is the one part of the pipeline that works on a repository with no concept at

recommendation: Add `quality-standards` to `appbuilder-standard` after scaffold, with a step in `build-plan` and `build-implement` that reads the index. Or state that the index exists only in the reverse flow.

title: ops-review is the longest skill and half of it is mechanical rule checks
detail: `ops-review` has 111 lines and 12 steps, the most of any skill. Steps 2, 3, 5 and 7 check structure, frontmatter, naming and decay against rules the contracts state mechanically. Three skills then act on the same acceptance state: `ops-review` turns a failing row red, `quality-release` refuses on a red row, `quality-review` re-runs `PASS` rows.

evidence.quote: slice is unfrozen, or commits or source files are empty, or an acceptance
Any red feature row means something claimed

recommendation: Move the mechanical half into a `check_concept.py` that `ops-review` calls, as `scripts/check.py` does for this collection. Keep judgement and the trace in the skill.

title: Release thresholds sit in the skill body, not in the evaluator contract
detail: `quality-release` fixes design average >= 7, accessibility >= 70 and LCP under 4s in steps 6 and 7. `evaluator.md` refers to a "pass threshold" and a "failure floor" and gives no number. The contract also says a skill that pins its own version of a rule will disagree with itself.

evidence.quote: a skill that pins its own version of it has

recommendation: Move the numeric thresholds to a table in `contracts/evaluator.md` and cite it at step 7.

title: identity.md contract lists tone; design-brand disclaims tone
detail: `concept_structure.md` says `identity.md` holds colours, fonts, tone and copy guidelines. `design-brand` says copy and tone of voice are not its job, and its step 5 lists no tone. No skill claims tone, so the contract names a content that nobody writes.

evidence.quote: colours, fonts, tone — and copy guidelines when asked for
Copy and tone of voice are not this skill's
`identity.md` carries the direction, the colour usage rules

recommendation: Write one sentence in `concept_structure.md` that names who owns tone and copy, or remove them from the `identity.md` line.
